description: C/C++ node: two-input AND gates written in C/C++. Top: wire push buttons from GPIO 4 (D2 on a D1 mini) and GPIO 5 (D1) to GND. Two GPIO input (change) nodes read them and are wired into the AND gate node, where they are bool variables BTN_A and BTN_B; it sends 1 while both are pressed, else 0, to the LED on GPIO 2. A second C/C++ node counts how often that happened with its own variable. Bottom: Switch A and Switch B are wired into one C/C++ node: send(SW_A && SW_B ? 1 : 0). C/C++ nodes do the logic only; reading and driving pins is done by the GPIO nodes. The code runs on the board only (a debug build flips the switches over MQTT); in ▶ Simulate the C/C++ nodes just pass values through.

config.vars:
bool pressedA = false, pressedB = false; // until a button reports
int last = -1; // result sent last (-1 = nothing yet)
int count = 0; // its own count: nothing to do with the gate's variables
config.message:
// GATE and PRETEND are the inputs wired into this node; `from` says which one sent.
if (value == "1") send(++count);

// SW_A and SW_B are the switches wired into this node: bool variables holding each one's latest value.
send(SW_A && SW_B ? 1 : 0);
